puzzles.title: The Exact Same Shortfall, Every Thursday
puzzles.scenario: At a small bookshop, the till never quite adds up at closing — but only on Thursdays, and always by the exact same small amount, even though the morning count that day is always correct.
puzzles.solution: A part-time employee who only works Thursdays treats himself to a coffee from the shop's small snack corner without ringing it up properly, always meaning to cover it out of his own pocket later, and always forgetting by his next shift. The amount is too small for him to ever think it matters.
puzzles.hint: Why that one day specifically, and who only works that day?

puzzles.matchTitle: Een handtekening, drie dagen na zijn overlijden
puzzles.title: A Signature, Three Days After His Death
puzzles.scenario: A charity has received the same donation letter every year for a decade from a wealthy donor, always with an identical, elegant signature. This year, the letter turns out to have been sent three days after his confirmed date of death.
puzzles.solution: Knowing his health was failing, the donor had a lawyer help him pre-sign and date an entire batch of letters years in advance, set to be mailed automatically every year regardless of his health, so the charity's funding would never visibly interrupt — not even in the year he died. The signature was real; it was just years older than the postmark suggested.
puzzles.hint: Is the signature fake, or is it just the timing of the mailing that's later than you'd expect?

puzzles.title: No Lock Forced, Yet Someone Broke In
puzzles.scenario: A burglary victim is certain the thief must have had a key, since there's no sign of forced entry. Yet the locksmith who rekeyed the house last month swears he handed a key to no one but the homeowner.
puzzles.solution: The homeowner's teenage son had quietly had a spare key cut at a hardware store months earlier and lost it at a party, on a keyring with a carelessly attached tag showing the house address. Whoever picked it up knew exactly which door it opened.
puzzles.hint: The locksmith only handed over one key. Has a second one appeared since, without him knowing?

puzzles.title: The Same Round Numbers for 'Office Supplies,' Year After Year
puzzles.scenario: A small business owner is suspected of tax fraud after auditors find years of suspiciously round, near-identical expenses for 'office supplies,' though he swears he never filed most of those invoices himself.
puzzles.solution: His bookkeeper had been embezzling from several small clients at once for years, padding each one's office-supplies line by a modest, easy-to-miss amount every month and routing the difference to himself through an intermediary account. It only surfaced when a new auditor compared several of the bookkeeper's clients side by side and noticed the identical pattern running across otherwise unrelated businesses.
puzzles.hint: Don't look at just one business. Look at who handles the books for several at once.

puzzles.matchTitle: Elf minuten herhaalde beelden, elke nacht op een ander moment
puzzles.title: Eleven Minutes of Looped Footage, at a Different Time Each Night
puzzles.scenario: A warehouse's security cameras have recorded flawless footage every night for months, until investigators discover that every night, at a different time, eleven minutes of the previous night's footage quietly loops in place of the live feed.
puzzles.solution: The night guard has been secretly delivering food through a gig app during the quiet hours of his shift, and set the system up months ago to loop a clean eleven-minute clip whenever he steps out. The timing varies because his delivery orders come in unpredictably. It was never meant to cover up a theft, just his side job, until a routine metadata check exposed it.
puzzles.hint: Is the gap in coverage planned around a crime, or around something else the guard does that night?

puzzles.matchTitle: Veertig kilo te zwaar, twee jaar lang genegeerd
puzzles.title: Forty Kilos Too Heavy, Ignored for Two Years
puzzles.scenario: A specific shipping container has cleared customs without issue on the same route for two years, yet it consistently arrives forty kilos heavier than its manifest states, though the seals never show tampering and nothing visibly has been added.
puzzles.solution: The container's refrigeration unit, custom-fitted for this route, hides a false bottom in its coolant reservoir where the exporter smuggles a dense, non-perishable good sealed in an inert gel. For two years the discrepancy was written off as a known quirk in that particular container's scale reading, until a new inspector got tired of the excuse and had it taken apart.
puzzles.hint: Don't search the cargo itself. Look at what's already built into the container and never gets checked.

puzzles.title: The Deposit Never Quite Adds Up
puzzles.scenario: A café owner counts and bags the exact right amount of cash for his weekly bank deposit himself, yet the amount that lands in his account is always rounded down to the nearest ten.
puzzles.solution: The teller who has processed his deposits for years pockets the small leftover change each time, assuming a business owner making regular deposits would never notice or bother reporting a few euros' difference. He only catches the pattern after a tax audit forces him to start keeping his own precise log.
puzzles.hint: Did the difference happen before he counted the money, or after, at the hands of whoever receives it?

puzzles.matchTitle: De vluchtauto staat precies waar de camera's niets zien
puzzles.title: The Getaway Car Sits Exactly Where the Cameras Can't See
puzzles.scenario: After a robbery, the getaway car turns up exactly where the traffic cameras have a blind spot. Investigators are stumped: every route to that spot should have passed at least one working camera, yet none logged a matching vehicle.
puzzles.solution: The thief never drove his own getaway car there at all. He rented an identical model through a car-sharing app, took camera-free back roads to the blind spot, and walked the last stretch to switch into his real car — which a cash-paid driver, who knew nothing, had already parked there hours earlier as an ordinary rental drop-off.
puzzles.hint: Don't look for the car the thief himself drove to the blind spot. Did he actually drive there at all?
